chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Her vocal approach from 1937 on and swing as her era
summary: She felt she had the same style but with more freedom; she belongs to the swing era.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yeah, well the material that I did with Ellis was, - to be frank, during the time that I was in the Le Ruban Bleu this is when I began to develop a style, an approach to pop music, to standards. And then of course, during the time I was at the Le Ruban Bleu I was working with Herman Chittison, you know, great piano player and accompanist. And it gave me a lot of scope there, and of course the Le Ruban Bleu was a very good Club to work in. It was a small, intimate club, and that I was working with a trio therefore I was not bound in by any other instruments, by piano, bass and guitar. We didn't even have drums.

But that was, during that time I was able to prove that I could do something else besides "Loch Lomand". But the Le Ruban Bleu was more or less an exclusive club and it wasn't one of those kind of places where everybody came. And in fact some of the musicians that I have known previously, musicians just didn't come to the Le Ruban Bleu, because they expected it to be too society type entertainment. The acts were, mostly the acts were from the theater, from legitimate

theater. They did alot of show music and alot of actors or performers who came in there to try out their cabaret type act. It was variety, of course. It was a different type setting. I was, I don't think I was classified as any particular type of singer. It was just because of the popularity and the - as I said before, my identification with "Loch Lomand". I was always billed as the 'Loch Lomand' lady." So you had to get that whether you wanted it or not.

Anyway, as far as your concern then, you, vocally you were doing more or less the same kind of thing from '37 up until, well you made your last records before, when were they, 1954 were the last two records you made.
Yeah, but with a little bit more freedom.
But the backing, you might have a Swing backing or you might have a big band backing as with Benny Carter.
I think it's more of a Swing backround. When I think of a jazz singer I think of singers, made the special material that they do, it's

identified with a jazz era. You must recall I came in when it was considered the Swing era. This was after jazz. The distinction being that there were certain types of songs that were part of the jazz repertoire. And it was mostly instrumental. So far as singers were concerned, singers were blue's singers, and I don't consider myself a blues singer. I may sound like a blue singer but I don't have a blue's singer's repertoire. The blues just doesn't appeal to me. That is, for me to sing. I can listen to it.
Even though those are the things that you listen to a great deal when you were young.
